es: Contar una respuesta de entrevista con situación, acción, resultado y lección, controlando pasado simple, pasado perfecto y presente perfecto.

teaching.es: La primavera pasada estaba a cargo del proyecto de reciclaje del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Situación: el pasado simple (was) sitúa la historia; in charge of indica tu papel.

teaching.es: Cuando llegué, los contenedores estaban llenos porque nadie había recogido el papel en una semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Pasado perfecto (had + participio) para lo ocurrido antes del momento que cuentas.

feedback.es: Nadie había recogido el papel antes de llegar: hecho anterior, pasado perfecto con had.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué aprendió la hablante.

choices.text: She learned to avoid school events.
She learned that posters are enough.
She learned to start by involving people.

feedback.es: Su lección está en el final: «I have always started with people, not posters».

origin.audio: Two years ago, I organised a food drive at school. At first, nobody had signed up, so I asked every class to choose a captain. As a result, we collected three hundred bags of food. Since then, I have always started with people, not posters.

choices.text: That project taught me to ask for help early.
That project had started before I arrived.
That project has run since last spring.

feedback.es: «Taught me to…» expresa la lección; las otras dos dan información de tiempo, no una enseñanza.

prompt.es: Escribe tu respuesta: situación, acción, resultado y lección.

answer.text: Last spring, I was in charge of the school recycling project. When I arrived, the bins were full because nobody had collected the paper for a week, and many students had stopped caring. My first step was to listen. I asked every class what was making recycling difficult, and most students said that nobody knew who was responsible. So I drew up a weekly rota and asked each class to choose a captain. I also wrote a short checklist for the captains, and I checked the bins myself every Friday during the first month. As a result, the bins have never been full again, and our recycling rate has doubled since then. Teachers have even started using the rota in other projects. The experience taught me that clear responsibility prevents most problems. It also taught me that a leader should listen before giving orders. Since then, I have used the same approach in every team I have joined.
accepted: Last spring, I was in charge of the school recycling project. When I arrived, the bins were full because nobody had collected the paper for a week, and many students had stopped caring. My first step was to listen. I asked every class what was making recycling difficult, and most students said that nobody knew who was responsible. So I drew up a weekly rota and asked each class to choose a captain. I also wrote a short checklist for the captains, and I checked the bins myself every Friday during the first month. As a result, the bins have never been full again, and our recycling rate has doubled since then. Teachers have even started using the rota in other projects. The experience taught me that clear responsibility prevents most problems. It also taught me that a leader should listen before giving orders. Since then, I have used the same approach in every team I have joined.

Two years ago, I was in charge of the charity concert at my school. When I joined the team, the posters were still not ready because nobody had booked the hall, and the students had already lost interest. I decided to start again with a clear plan. I made a checklist, I asked each class to choose a captain, and I called the music teacher to ask for help. We booked the hall within two days and sold every ticket in a week. As a result, the concert has become a yearly tradition, and the school has raised twice as much money since then. The experience taught me that a simple plan gives people confidence. I also learned that asking for help early saves time. Today, I use the same method whenever I start a new project.

feedback.es: Una respuesta completa sitúa la historia, cuenta tu acción, da un resultado que sigue vigente y cierra con una lección.

origin.text: En una entrevista para un programa de liderazgo te piden: «Cuéntame una ocasión en que lideraste un proyecto». Escribe unas 130–270 palabras: situación y acción en pasado, un hecho anterior con pasado perfecto, un resultado vigente con presente perfecto y la lección aprendida.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ha cambiado hasta hoy.

choices.text: The garden has given vegetables every summer.

feedback.es: El resultado vigente es «has produced vegetables every summer since then»: el jardín sigue dando verduras.

origin.audio: Last year, I was in charge of the school garden. When I arrived, nobody had watered the plants for a month. I made a watering rota, and as a result, the garden has produced vegetables every summer since then.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase sitúa algo anterior al momento de la historia?

choices.text: By the time I arrived, the team was leaving soon.
By the time I arrived, the team will already leave.
By the time I arrived, the team had already left.

feedback.es: Had already left indica que el equipo se fue antes de que llegara el narrador: pasado perfecto.

prompt.es: Completa: «Desde entonces, hemos duplicado las ventas.»

feedback.es: Since then y un efecto que sigue hoy exigen presente perfecto: have doubled.

origin.text: Since then, we ___ doubled our sales.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La situación me enseñó a repartir el trabajo.»

answer.text: The situation taught me to share the work

feedback.es: La lección se introduce con taught me to…, seguido de la idea que aprendiste.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cuenta un resultado que sigue vigente hoy?

choices.text: Since then, the club has gained forty members.
Since then, the club gained forty members.
Before then, the club had gained forty members.

feedback.es: Since then + presente perfecto muestra un resultado que llega hasta hoy: has gained.
